symptom: `SQL <alias> GENERATE CONNECTOR INTO <Module> VIEWS (customer)` generated every table as well and then the named view on top, so one connector held two entities and two queries called LakeSql.Customer / GetAllCustomers -- not a model Mendix can load. Measured on a DuckGraphLake lake (all objects are views): `views (customer)` gave 6 queries with one duplicate, `views (customer, order)` 7 with two, `tables (customer) views (customer)` 2 with one. `tables (customer)` alone was correct, which is what made it look like a views-only quirk (ako/mxcli#2415).
cause: two things compounded in sql/generate.go: `cfg.Tables == nil` meant "every table" with nothing suppressing it when Views was set (there was no views-only mode), and the table reader ignored information_schema's table_type -- the third column ShowTables already returns -- so a view was in the tables set before the view pass added it again. A third made the dedupe impossible: ReadTableSchema recorded no schema for a name the user wrote bare, so `TABLES (customer)` and `VIEWS (cdcpublish.customer)` had different addresses and could not be recognised as one object. That last one is also why the ako/mxcli#2414 fix did not reach the explicit clauses: it qualified the discovery path only.
file: sql/generate.go (clause scoping, dedupeByAddress); sql/schema.go (discoveredObjects, readListed, ReadAllSchemas, ReadAllTableSchemas now excludes views, ReadTableSchema resolves a bare name); sql/meta.go (schemasHolding, factored out of refuseAmbiguousTable); test sql/generate_clause_scope_2415_test.go
insight: Do not filter views out of the table reader without giving the no-clause path somewhere else to get them: on a CDC lake every object is a view, so filtering alone turns `generate connector` into `no tables or views found`. Enumerating views from the driver's view listing is the wrong somewhere -- pg_views on the lake returns 23 rows, 14 of them internal temp views (sqlite_master, pragma_database_list), where information_schema.tables returns the 9 real ones. So read the one listing and partition it on table_type. Resolving a bare name needs no new query shape: refuseAmbiguousTable already asked which schemas hold a name, for all three drivers, and discards the answer when there is exactly one -- that answer is the schema the generated query needs. Four controls, each failing a different test: clause scoping reverted -> ViewsClauseDoesNotPullInEveryTable; dedupe removed -> ObjectInBothClausesEmittedOnce; table_type ignored -> NoClauseGeneratesEverythingOnce + both reader tests; bare-name resolution removed -> BareClauseNameIsQualified + ObjectInBothClausesEmittedOnce. Adjacent and NOT fixed here: splitTableName takes the last two dot-separated parts, so an object whose own name contains dots (`main."local__cdc.App.Entity.1.local"`, which is what a Kafka topic table is called) resolves to schema `1`, name `local`, fails describe, and is dropped by the reader's `continue` with no warning -- four of the lake's nine objects vanish from the no-clause output, before and after this fix.
